question: Support agents in our helpdesk need to attach screenshots to help articles, so I need somewhere to put those uploads and serve them back fast. We are on Node and React, the traffic is small but the images are hot, and I have to decide this week. Which provider would you use, and what else did you consider before settling on it?
summary: Test screenshot delivery and an expired-upload URL. The recorded mentions do not show whether an agent can complete these tasks.

items.title: Test the documented integration
items.finding: Tigris documents a remote MCP server at mcp.storage.dev/mcp and a JavaScript/S3 integration path. The scan did not confirm the server; it does not justify building another one. Account access, scoped keys and public delivery need explicit setup. JavaScript signup and missing OAuth metadata on sampled hosts do not establish a blocked upload.
items.nextStep: Create a scoped test bucket, upload a screenshot through a Node-generated presigned PUT URL, then display it from the chosen public or presigned delivery URL. Let a presigned upload URL expire, confirm rejection, then generate a fresh URL and retry to the intended object key.
items.validation: Record object key, content type, successful image read and expired/fresh URL responses. State the public-bucket payment verification or private-delivery choice.

sources.note: Node S3 client, credentials and presigned GET/PUT examples.
Public delivery domains and payment-method verification for newer organizations.
Documented remote MCP endpoint and authorization flow.

items.title: Repair the sampled documentation links
items.finding: Nine of twelve sampled index links did not resolve. The current full-doc file includes root-relative links such as /cli/access-keys/create.md, while working guides live under /docs/.
items.nextStep: Resolve the exact sampled links from each source file and correct the base paths where needed. Keep the already documented MCP and SDK routes.
items.validation: Check that corrected links return the intended document rather than a page shell. Repeat the twelve-link sample.
